item.title: US Agrees to Buy at Least 850 More Lockheed F-35 Fighter Jets
item.description: The Pentagon plans to buy at least 850 additional Lockheed Martin Corp. F-35 fighter jets, in what would be the biggest contract in the program’s quarter-century history that signals the stealth warplane will remain a major part of the US arsenal for many years.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Dallas' Perot Museum Places $185 Million Bet on Science
item.description: Dallas' Perot Museum of Nature and Science plans a $185 million expansion, according to Linda Silver, the museum's chief executive officer. Texas' growing dependence on so-called STEM careers in science, technology and math adds urgency to the need for more early interest in the field, Silver tells Bloomberg's Julie Fine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cockroach Party Evolves Into Indian Prime Minister Modi’s Opposition
item.description: India’s prime minister isn’t likely to give in to the CJP easily.
item.dc:creator: Dan Strumpf

item.title: Capitol Rioters Pardoned by Trump for Police Assaults Want US Payouts
item.description: Nearly 200 people granted clemency by Trump for Jan. 6 charges are suing for US compensation, including dozens convicted of attacking or impeding law enforcement
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: UK Politicians Are Testing Their Messages on AI-Generated Focus Groups
item.description: UK politicians looking to gauge how British voters will react to their policies have a new cohort on which to test their ideas: AI-generated focus groups.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Reid

item.title: Italian Truckers Press Blockades as Vegetables Start to Rot
item.description: Truckers in Italy continued to block roads in the country’s south on Thursday, with fishing fleets in the port of Ancona also idled to protest high diesel prices.
item.dc:creator: Alessandra Migliaccio and Selena Frasson

item.title: Malaysian Court Stops Opposition Bloc’s Deregistration: Edge
item.description: A Malaysian court has halted the deregistration of the country’s main opposition coalition, effectively allowing it to contest the upcoming Malacca state election, The Edge reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Ram Anand

item.title: Tanzanian Opposition Leader Charged With Treason Over Protests
item.description: A Tanzanian court charged a senior opposition figure with treason, adding to a widening crackdown a week ahead of the first anniversary of deadly election protests.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Suu Kyi Speaks With Son for First Time Since 2021 Myanmar Coup
item.description: Aung San Suu Kyi spoke with her son for the first time in more than five years, marking a rare instance of family contact for the ousted Myanmar leader since she was detained following the 2021 military coup.
item.dc:creator: Khine Lin Kyaw

item.title: Brazil’s João, Walter Moreira Salles Back Lula Over Bolsonaro in Runoff
item.description: Two brothers from Brazil’s richest family have emerged as opponents of right-wing presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of Sunday’s closely fought runoff election.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Rochabrún

item.title: Bhaskar Sunkara Thinks the Market Has a Place Under Socialism
item.description: In September, Gallup released a poll that showed that 43% percent of Americans viewed socialism positively, the highest approval since Gallup began the poll back in 2010. Since Zohran Mamdani won the NYC mayoral election, the left has made a number of gains across national politics. As a longtime DSA member and veteran of leftist media, Bhaskar Sunkara is one of socialism's leading advocates, and he's spent much of his career charting what a socialist economy in America might look like. Unlike some other leftists, he believes the market has a place. In fact, he thinks markets and entrepreneurs are an objective good in society. He proposes a vision of so-called "market socialism" in his recent co-authored book The Blueprint, and he lays out this system for us in today's episode. We talk about how many features of capitalism — from small businesses to monetary policy — might be remade under socialist principles. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Pulls Diplomats From Saudi as Houthi, Iran Tensions Worsen
item.description: The US ordered some diplomats and their families to leave Saudi Arabia because of the threat from Houthi militants, as the Iran-backed group carried out more strikes from Yemen.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Elimam, Courtney McBride and Eric Martin

item.title: Disclosure: The SEC Roots Out Golf on Taxpayer Dime
item.description: How do government agencies ferret out waste and abuse? Jason and Matt learn what happened when the SEC got a tip that some of its workers were spending office hours on the golf course. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan’s Top Union Group Calls For 6% Wage Increases in 2027
item.description: Japan’s largest labor union federation will push for wage increases of around 6% in next year’s pay negotiations, seeking to build on recent gains as the government targets sustained pay rises to help drive consumer spending and boost economic growth.
item.dc:creator: Erica Yokoyama

item.title: AI Trade Jitters Return, Oil Gains After Deadly Saudi Attacks
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Berlin, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
On today's show, global stocks fell after a mixed start to US tech earnings failed to calm nerves around the AI trade. Meta doubled down on its investment plans, boosting its capital spending forecast for the year.
Oil advanced after deadly Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. Two people were killed in a drone strike on an Aramco oil field and one person died in an attack on an airport. The US has ordered non-emergency personnel and their families to leave the country.
Today's guests: Francisco Blanch, Bank of America, Head of Global Commodities & Derivatives Research; Christian Keller, Barclays, Head of Economic Research. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Putin Gets Praised as 'Humanitarian' by Witkoff
item.description: The Trump administration praised Russian President Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian” for releasing a detained US citizen. Steve Witkoff complimented Putin in Russia as he secured the release of Stephen Hubbard, an American teacher convicted there four years ago of fighting for Ukraine. Bloomberg's Anthony Halpin reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Paris Bans Protests in Some High-Profile Areas on Thursday
item.description: Paris police banned protests and demonstrations Thursday in some areas of the city, including around the presidential palace, along the Champs-Elysées and near other tourist sites, citing the risk of violence.
item.dc:creator: Alan Katz and Alessandra Migliaccio

item.title: EU Nears Securitization Reform in Bid to Unleash Billions
item.description: The European Union reached a provisional agreement to overhaul rules governing the bloc’s securitization markets, a deal that would unleash billions of euros to finance initiatives in key areas such as defense and climate resilience.
item.dc:creator: Esteban Duarte and Laura Noonan

item.title: Witkoff Praises Putin After Detained US Citizen Released
item.description: The Trump administration praised Russian President Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian” for releasing a detained US citizen, the latest White House move to curry favor with Russia in its efforts to end the war in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Iain Marlow

item.title: Burnham Floats Removing Gas Bills Fee to Blunt Price Surge
item.description: The UK government is looking to remove standing charges on gas bills, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, as part of the Labour government’s efforts to blunt the impact of surging energy costs.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain and Eamon Akil Farhat
